newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait state wages to consume oil revenue by 2003/04.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait state wages to consume oil revenue by 2003/04.

text.p: Kuwait's state wages are expected to account for the Gulf state's income from its main revenue earner, oil, in the year 2003/04 (July-June), an official said in remarks published on Thursday.

"According to projections salaries will swallow up the country's oil earnings by the advent of fiscal year 2003-2004," the Arab Times reported Waleed al-Wouhaib, general coordinator for restructuring of the state apparatus, as saying.
According to the proposed 1997/98 state budget figures, wages would make 29.4 percent of total spending and 50 percent of oil revenue, which accounts for 80 percent of total revenue.
"This according to him was due to distortion in the labour market, which he predicted would lead to the eventual collapse of the state's development plans," it said.
Kuwaitis make up 1.75 percent of the private sector labour force which consists mainly of cheaper Asian and Arab workers.
Kuwait, which produces about two million barrels of crude per day, has about a tenth of the world oil reserves.

Kuwait, with a total population of two million people, has about 3,000 unemployed Kuwaitis of the national population of about 720,000. But parliamentarians and economists have often voiced fears of an emerging unemployment problem.
The state is obliged by law to provide a job for every Kuwaiti seeking one. Kuwaitis prefer state jobs which guarantee higher pay, early retirement and job security.
